UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE, Plaintiff, v. KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6, Defendants. ____________________________________/ | Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

PLAINTIFF’S ADMINISTRATIVE MOTION FOR EXPEDITED BRIEFING, PRIORITY DETERMINATION, AND A DEFINED DECISION SCHEDULE FOR THE TWO RULE 26(d)(1) APPLICATIONS

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1), Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 1, 7(b)(1), and 78(b), and the Court’s authority to manage its docket, and, for the alternative referral requested below, under 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(A), for fixed briefing dates, a defined submission event, an identified decision-maker, and a defined determination date for two applications: Plaintiff’s Motion Under Rule 26(d)(1) for Present Authorization to Serve One Interrogatory on NCMEC Concerning Plaintiff’s Full Legal Name (ECF No. [___]) (the “NCMEC Application”) and Plaintiff’s Motion Under Rule 26(d)(1) for Present Authorization to Serve Two Interrogatories on Meta Concerning Plaintiff’s Full Legal Name and Facebook Account (ECF No. [___]) (the “Meta Application”) (together, the “Applications”). Plaintiff requests an expedited schedule for deciding the two applications, not discovery authorization through this administrative motion. This motion is the “Administrative Motion.”

Neither Application requests shortened briefing through its own prayer for relief. This separate Administrative Motion requests that change on notice to all appearing parties. The existing briefing periods govern unless the Court orders otherwise.

A Memorandum in Support, the Administrative Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine (“Admin. Decl.”), Proposed Order 4A, alternative Proposed Order 4B, Proposed Interim Order 4C, and a Notice of Waiver of Oral Argument and Request for Prompt Determination on the Papers accompany this Administrative Motion. “Administrative” describes the case-management relief requested. It invokes no other district’s rule and claims no exemption from Local Civil Rule 7.

I.	THE APPLICATIONS AND THE PRESENT POSTURE

1.	The Applications and the respondents. The NCMEC Application seeks authorization of one interrogatory to Defendant National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (“NCMEC”): whether NCMEC holds any CyberTipline report, received from any reporting party between July 1, 2022 and April 22, 2026, inclusive, that as originally received contained or otherwise identified the full legal name “Marvelle J. Ballentine.” The Meta Application seeks authorization of two independent interrogatories to Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”): whether Meta submitted to NCMEC in that period any CyberTipline report that, as submitted, contained or otherwise identified that full legal name; and whether Meta submitted to NCMEC in that period any CyberTipline report in connection with the Facebook account associated with Plaintiff and enforced against on or about July 4, 2022. The Memorandum in Support reproduces the questions. Each permits “Yes,” “No,” or “Unable to determine after reasonable inquiry,” a concise qualification necessary for accuracy, and specific objections; none seeks report production. NCMEC is the sole respondent to its interrogatory. Meta is the sole respondent to its two interrogatories. Defendant Katie Hall may oppose or join an opposition to the NCMEC Application and receives no interrogatory. Neither Application depends on the other.

2.	The existing posture. On October 7, 2026, Magistrate Judge Davis denied Plaintiff’s earlier three-interrogatory and four-interrogatory requests “as premature,” stating that “discovery has not officially begun in this case” and that “currently there is no Scheduling Order in this case.” ECF No. 84 at 1–2. On October 29, 2026, Magistrate Judge Fitzpatrick denied Plaintiff’s scheduling and Rule 26(f) motions without prejudice, stating: “Here, the record reflects that the District Judge has chosen to refrain from beginning any discovery until resolution of the pending motions to dismiss.” ECF No. 108 at 2. This Administrative Motion does not ask the Court to vacate either order. Plaintiff’s objections and other requests concerning those orders remain pending on their own terms. See paragraph 10.

3.	Present consequences. The Administrative Declaration describes Plaintiff’s circumstances as of November 7, 2026: his intention to retain counsel and his reluctance to risk another refusal while the association between his full legal name and CyberTipline reports remains unresolved; the effect of that unresolved association on his willingness to participate openly in professional networking, business development, technology incubators, accelerator programs, and founder fellowships; and stress affecting his daily work and family responsibilities. Admin. Decl. ¶¶ 5–11. Accurate sworn reporting information would inform his decisions about seeking counsel and participating openly in professional activities. Id. ¶ 12.

4.	The need for a separate timetable. Each Application requests prompt determination on the papers. Neither shortens the opposition or reply period, fixes a submission event, or sets a decision date; a motion cannot do those things for itself. Without an order, Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1) supplies 14 calendar days for an opposition and six calendar days for a reply, and no rule supplies a date by which either Application will be decided. ECF No. 108 identifies the end of the deferral as “resolution of the pending motions to dismiss” and identifies no date for deciding a request for an exception. ECF No. 108 at 2.

5.	Paper submission. The November 5, 2026 docket entry states: “Per RDA’s chambers, motions set for 12/16/2026 will be decided on the papers; no oral argument will be heard.” It terminated the December 16 hearing setting for the motions then set. It set no decision date for the two Applications and did not expressly allocate their determination. Plaintiff waives oral argument on this Administrative Motion and requests court-directed determination on the papers under Rule 78(b) and Local Civil Rules 7(E) and 7(J). A separate Notice accompanies this Administrative Motion. Each Application carries its own waiver.

II.	THE REQUESTED SCHEDULE

6.	Prompt administrative action and the interim procedure. Plaintiff requests determination of this Administrative Motion on notice to all appearing parties, preferably within two business days after its service on all appearing parties, so that the requested briefing dates can operate prospectively. This is a request for action by the Court, not a unilateral response deadline. If the Court requires administrative submissions before ruling, Plaintiff requests entry of Proposed Interim Order 4C: a fixed opposition date two business days after notice of that order, a fixed reply date one business day after the opposition deadline, and determination immediately after the Administrative Motion becomes submitted. A “business day” is a day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday as defined in Rule 6(a)(6); the day of the triggering event is excluded. The interim procedure takes effect only by court order. This Administrative Motion creates no deadline and does not treat silence within any period as consent. The interim procedure concerns timing, submission, and routing, not the merits of discovery. Plaintiff serves the entire package on every appearing party and requests no ex parte determination of anything.

7.	Fixed-date briefing and submission. For each Application separately, Plaintiff requests fixed calendar dates: an opposition date providing seven calendar days after service of the complete Application to every appearing party served with it, and a reply date three calendar days after that opposition date, each selected under Rule 6(a). Plaintiff may reply earlier. One reply addresses every timely opposition to that Application; a joint opposition by NCMEC and Hall is addressed in the NCMEC reply; a single paper addressing both Applications is addressed in each Application’s one reply without merging the schedules; separate opposition papers create no additional reply rounds. No additional days attach to the fixed dates because of the method of service, and the dates govern only the briefing of the Applications. Plaintiff requests that each brief subject to the fixed dates be accompanied by a contemporaneous electronic courtesy copy to the other parties, in addition to service under Rule 5, at jayballentine@protonmail.com for Plaintiff; courtesy delivery is not consent to electronic service and starts no period. Each Application becomes submitted when its opposition deadline has passed and Plaintiff has filed and served the authorized reply or the reply deadline has passed. If no opposition is filed, the Application becomes submitted when its opposition deadline passes. Neither Application awaits briefing or determination of the other. An early reply does not close another party’s opposition period, the Court may act earlier when procedurally appropriate, and a late filing does not automatically restart briefing or the determination period.

8.	Determination, routing, and sequencing. Plaintiff requests determination of each Application within seven calendar days after it becomes submitted, or another date certain expressly fixed by the Court, and, if the Court fixes a different date, that the order state the substituted date and the reason for the departure. The seven-day period is requested case-management relief, not an existing statutory deadline; its passage produces no automatic grant, sanction, or finding. An Application fully briefed when the scheduling order enters keeps its completed briefing and is treated as submitted upon entry. If shortened briefing can no longer operate prospectively, Plaintiff requests an order fixing submission, routing, and a determination date on the briefing as it then stands. Completed briefing remains complete. Plaintiff requests this relief without a further motion.

Plaintiff requests that Judge Alston determine both Applications. ECF No. 108 at 2 attributes the deferral of discovery to the District Judge; Plaintiff describes that attribution as the order states it, and his request to clarify or correct that passage, ECF Nos. 122–123, remains pending. In the alternative, Plaintiff requests an express referral under 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(A) and Local Civil Rule 72 authorizing the assigned Magistrate Judge to determine whether to permit the requested limited exception to the deferral described in ECF No. 108, including any service and response terms, with the schedule in paragraphs 7 and 8 carried with the referral, completed briefing preserved, and no new hearing setting. If the assigned Magistrate Judge regards that deferral as reserving the exception question to the District Judge, Plaintiff requests that the Magistrate Judge state that understanding and present the request to Judge Alston on the existing submissions. Plaintiff requests an order identifying the judicial officer authorized to determine the exception. Any reserved question should be presented to the District Judge on the existing submissions.

To the extent an adverse disposition would depend on the specific reporting fact addressed by an application’s Exhibit A, Plaintiff requests that the Court resolve that authorization request before or expressly within that disposition. The requested timetable does not depend on that provision. The provision adds protection for the identified situation only.

III.	CONFERRAL, PRESERVATION, AND SEVERABILITY

9.	Conferral. Plaintiff makes this statement under Local Civil Rule 37(E) and does not contend that the word “administrative” removes this Administrative Motion from that rule. [Complete from the November 9, 2026 conferences or documented attempts. Do not presume that a conference occurred or that any position was taken.] On [date], at [time] Eastern, Plaintiff conferred by [telephone / in person] with [name], counsel for NCMEC and Hall. Plaintiff presented the seven-day opposition period, the three-day reply period, the seven-day determination request, paper submission, and the retention-or-referral alternatives, and asked counsel’s position on each. Counsel for NCMEC and Hall stated: [record the position on each item separately; record any different timetable proposed and the reason counsel gave; state agreement only if counsel expressed it]. On [date], at [time] Eastern, Plaintiff conferred by [telephone / in person] with [name], counsel for Meta, presented the same items, and asked counsel’s position on each. Counsel for Meta stated: [the corresponding facts, separately attributed]. [If a conference with either counsel did not occur, state each attempt, its date, time, and means, and any response.] Plaintiff reports each position as counsel stated it and infers no position on the schedule from a position on the merits of either Application. Admin. Decl. ¶¶ 13–14.

10.	Preservation and independence. ECF No. 109 ¶ 11 asked the Court to preserve immediate determination of independent or threshold issues and independently warranted relief. This Administrative Motion is consistent with that request and does not alter the sequence requested there. Plaintiff maintains ECF Nos. 89–90, 93, 97–99, 112–113, and 118–123 on their own grounds and reargues none of them here. ECF No. 114-2 is a proposed pleading accompanying a pending amendment motion. ECF No. 116 is a separate request for an agency determination and alternative Rule 56(g) findings. ECF Nos. 133–135 are the settlement-referral proceedings. None of those matters is a prerequisite to consideration of the Applications, and this Administrative Motion asks for no stay of anything. Neither Application depends on disposition of this Administrative Motion, and neither Application awaits the other. This Administrative Motion does not rename either Application as renewed and asserts no Rule 54(b) ground. Until the Court directs otherwise, existing deadlines govern; filing this Administrative Motion is not itself an order shortening time.

11.	Severability. Denial of shortened briefing does not dispose of the requests for paper submission, routing, priority consideration, or a defined determination date. Disposition of the administrative motion does not dispose of either discovery application. Each request in the prayer is made separately and may be granted without the others.

PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff requests that the Court enter Proposed Order 4A or, in the alternative, Proposed Order 4B, and, only if the Court requires administrative submissions before ruling, Proposed Interim Order 4C, and that the Court:

(a)	determine this Administrative Motion on notice to all appearing parties, preferably within two business days after its service on all appearing parties, or, if administrative submissions are required, enter Proposed Interim Order 4C with a fixed opposition date two business days after notice of that order, a fixed reply date one business day after the opposition deadline, and determination immediately after submission;

(b)	fix, for each Application, a calendar date for any opposition providing seven calendar days after service of the complete Application and a calendar date for Plaintiff’s one reply three calendar days after that opposition date, as fixed deadlines to which no additional days attach because of the method of service, with contemporaneous electronic courtesy copies of each brief in addition to service under Rule 5;

(c)	provide that each Application becomes submitted on the terms stated in paragraph 7, independently of the other and without a hearing, and will be determined on the papers;

(d)	determine each Application within seven calendar days after it becomes submitted, or fix another date certain and state the substituted date and the reason for the departure; treat an Application fully briefed at entry as submitted upon entry; and, if shortened briefing can no longer operate prospectively, fix submission, routing, and a determination date on the briefing as it then stands, without a further motion;

(e)	retain determination of both Applications in the District Judge or, in the alternative, expressly refer both Applications under 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(A) and Local Civil Rule 72 to the assigned Magistrate Judge with authority to determine the requested limited exception to the deferral described in ECF No. 108, including any service and response terms, with the schedule in (b) through (d) intact and completed briefing preserved, and in either case identify the judicial officer authorized to determine the exception;

(f)	provide that, to the extent an adverse disposition would depend on the specific reporting fact addressed by an Application’s Exhibit A, the Court will resolve that authorization request before or expressly within that disposition;

(g)	provide that no deadline imposed by the order operates retroactively, that completed briefing remains complete, that the order does not automatically restart briefing, revive an expired deadline, or enlarge an existing deadline, that any prospective replacement date is stated expressly in the order, and that entry of the order neither authorizes discovery nor starts any interrogatory-response period;

(h)	provide that the order disposes of this Administrative Motion only to the extent expressly stated and does not determine either Application’s merits or dispose of any other pending motion or objection; and

(i)	treat each request in (a) through (h) as severable.
